reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or individual campus specifications. The disclosed facts are the location in Dallas County as part of a three-county West Des Moines campus, reported investment of $1.5-2 billion, and plans for a sixth data center building codenamed Ruthenium. Without published megawatts, this facility cannot be ranked against others by consumption, though it is part of a multi-building campus operated by a major cloud provider.

Iowa has 52 mapped data center facilities in OpenStreetMap, but only two operators publish power figures, totaling 18 MW across the state. This campus ranks third by published capacity in Iowa, a ranking that reflects the state's sparse disclosure rather than verified consumption. The campus is one of the few in Iowa whose operator has named it as a strategic investment site.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on information Microsoft has chosen not to disclose. The reported investment scale and multi-building expansion plan suggest material scale, but the absence of published power data means this site's actual contribution to grid demand and AI compute capacity cannot be read from public facts. The ranking itself indicates that Iowa's data center capacity is mostly unmeasured.
